gen.title: Pauses and thermal changes in the vertical structure

cards.stem: What term is used for the boundaries where layers show the greatest changes in thermal characteristics and related properties?
cards.quote: Each of the layers are bounded by "pauses" where the greatest changes in thermal characteristics, chemical composition, movement, and density occur.
cards.hint: Recall the name given to transition zones between layers.

cards.stem: How does the thermal structure change vertically after high energy radiation is absorbed in this upper layer?
cards.quote: Because of this absorption, the temperature increases with height.
cards.hint: Think about the effect of absorption on the thermal profile.

cards.stem: What is the name of the transition layer at the bottom of the stratosphere?
cards.quote: The transition layer at the bottom of the stratosphere is called the tropopause.
cards.hint: This boundary separates the lowest two layers.

cards.stem: What happens to the air as gas density decreases with height in the lower atmosphere?
cards.quote: As the density of the gases in this layer decrease with height, the air becomes thinner.
cards.hint: Consider how density relates to air thickness.
